findings.title: Backup code alone can log in if any TOTP field is sent
findings.body: Password verification in credentials authorize runs only when `user.password` is set and `credentials.totpCode` is empty. The new branch then treats any non-empty `backupCode` as a full login: it decrypts the stored codes, and on a match it burns that code and returns a session. It never checks the password itself. A caller who knows only a backup code (the plaintext file this feature downloads as cal-backup-codes.txt, a clipboard copy, or the setup response) can POST email, `totpCode` set to any non-empty value such as "1", and that backup code, and get a session without the password. The normal UI often avoids this only because it clears `totpCode` before submit; the credentials endpoint does not. The code is also consumed on that request, so the attacker takes the account and destroys a recovery code. Verify the password inside this branch whenever the user has one, before accepting or burning the code. Do not rely on the earlier `!credentials.totpCode` gate.

findings.title: One-time backup codes can be replayed or restored under concurrent logins
findings.body: After a backup code matches, the handler nulls that array slot and writes the re-encrypted list with a plain `prisma.user.update` on user id. The read, check, and write are not in a transaction and the update is not conditional on the previous ciphertext. Two parallel logins with the same code can both see it as unused and both receive sessions. Two parallel logins with different codes can also lose an update: the later write is based on a stale array and can put a just-consumed code back. Backup codes are documented as single-use, but that is not enforced. Consume the code with a row lock or compare-and-swap on the stored ciphertext so only one request can spend a given code.

findings.title: Valid backup codes are rejected unless they match lowercase hex exactly
findings.body: Stored codes are lowercase hex from `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`. Login compares with `indexOf` after removing only "-" characters. The same check is in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` at the `replaceAll("-", "")` / `indexOf` call. There is no `toLowerCase()` or trim. The entry field (`apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx`) uses placeholder "XXXXX-XXXXX", which reads as uppercase, and does not set `autoCapitalize="none"` or `autoCorrect="off"`, so mobile keyboards will capitalize the first character. Pasting a line from the downloaded file often includes a trailing newline or space; a code entered as uppercase or with whitespace will not match and the user gets "incorrect backup code" for a real code. Normalize by stripping whitespace and dashes and lowercasing before compare, on both login and disable.

findings.title: Closing the backup-code dialog does not finish setup or keep the codes
findings.body: TOTP enable is committed on the server before the backup codes are shown (`setStep(DisplayBackupCodes)` only after enable returns 200). The plaintext codes exist only in that earlier setup response and in React state; nothing in this PR can show them again, and `setup.ts` rejects another setup with TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled once 2FA is on. The dialog still uses the parent `onOpenChange` with no guard. Cancel is hidden on this step, but Escape, overlay click, and the dialog close control still dismiss it. Only the Close button calls `onEnable()` (and `resetState()`). The new e2e expects the security switch to become checked only after that Close click, so a dismiss leaves the settings UI showing 2FA off while the account has 2FA on. If the modal unmounts or the user leaves the page without using Copy/Download, the codes are gone and cannot be recovered without the authenticator. Block dismiss on this step until the user confirms the codes are saved, or call the same completion path as Close, and offer a way to regenerate codes while 2FA is already on.

findings.title: Missing-backup-codes error points at a settings flow that does not exist
findings.body: The new string is "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." Login and disable show it when 2FA is on and `backupCodes` is null (every account that enabled 2FA before this migration, and any account whose codes were never stored). There is no settings control or API in this PR to generate codes afterward: `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` returns TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled if 2FA is already on, and codes are only returned during that setup call. A user who lost the authenticator and follows this message cannot generate codes and cannot sign in. The copy should not tell them to do something the product cannot do.

findings.title: Copy toast claims success even if clipboard write fails
findings.body: The Copy handler calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` and immediately shows the success toast without awaiting or catching the promise. `writeText` rejects when clipboard permission is denied, the document is not focused, or `navigator.clipboard` is unavailable, and that rejection is unhandled. The user is told "Backup codes copied!" and can close the only screen that shows the codes without a copy actually existing. Await the write, and show an error toast (and do not claim success) if it fails.

findings.title: Tests never prove a backup code can log in or that it is single-use
findings.body: The first enable test still ends by waiting on the 2FA switch after OTP submit and does not click `backup-codes-close`. After this PR that submit leaves the backup-code dialog open and does not run `onEnable`, so the switch is not updated; the assertion above is the one the new FIXME says passes even when the switch is unchecked. The second test only checks that a download is named cal-backup-codes.txt, that a success toast appears, and that Close checks the switch. It does not read the file or clipboard (those checks are TODOs) and never submits a backup code. Nothing covers login with a backup code, rejection of a wrong or reused code, or disabling 2FA with a backup code, which is the behavior this PR adds. A break in comparison, consumption, or the password check would still leave CI green.
